name: Cicaplast Baume B5

card.summary: La Roche-Posay's panthenol-based repair balm, used to calm and help heal irritated, dry or post-treatment skin so it looks less red and rough.
card.note: Often used after retinoids, peels and dermatological procedures.

quick.overview:
Cicaplast Baume B5 is a soothing, repairing balm from the French pharmacy brand La Roche-Posay. People reach for it when skin is irritated, chapped, reddened or recovering from a procedure, because calmer, barrier-intact skin looks smoother and less inflamed.

A 2025 study in the European Journal of Dermatology followed 2,337 people using the B5+ version for skin lesions needing regenerative care, including superficial wounds, irritative dermatitis and skin recovering from treatments such as those for actinic keratosis, and reported improvement in clinical signs.
quick.how: It is smoothed over irritated areas once or twice daily, or applied as the last step of a night routine over a retinoid or after peels, lasers and shaving. In looksmax routines it appears as a cheap barrier-repair step alongside gentle cleansers and sunscreen, and sometimes as a lip balm variant.
quick.risks: The balm is designed for sensitive skin and is generally well tolerated, though any product can cause reactions, and it is a rich texture that some find heavy on oily skin. Wounds that are deep, infected or not healing are for clinicians to evaluate.

lead: Cicaplast Baume B5, now sold as Cicaplast Baume B5+, is a soothing and repairing balm made by La Roche-Posay, a French pharmacy skin-care brand that belongs to L'Oréal's Dermatological Beauty division [5][6]. The balm is positioned for dry, irritated or sensitive skin on the face, lips and body, and for care after dermatological procedures [5].

People use it to make irritated, dry or post-treatment skin look and feel better: less redness, less flaking, less tightness. In appearance communities it turns up in routines built around retinoids, where users layer a repair balm to manage dryness, and as a follow-on after in-office treatments [2][3]. The product's headline ingredients are panthenol (vitamin B5), madecassoside, a Centella asiatica extract, and a prebiotic complex the brand calls Tribioma [5].

A 2025 study published in the European Journal of Dermatology enrolled 2,337 patients needing regenerative skin care and found significant improvement in all clinical parameters after the recommended period of use, with at least 64.9 percent improving by a grade on each symptom [1]. Cancer-supportive skin-care guidance from the NECOM group has also included the balm in a daily regimen for patients with treatment-related skin reactions [4].

angle.text: It is used on irritated, dry or recovering skin to reduce visible redness and roughness. People use it on a retinoid routine or after procedures so skin looks smoother while it recovers.

paras: Cicaplast Baume B5+ is a multi-purpose balm positioned for skin that is irritated or needs regenerative care. The 2025 European Journal of Dermatology study describes the product as a prebiotic, panthenol-containing repair balm [1]. La Roche-Posay's own product page describes it as suitable for babies, children and adults, with a non-greasy balm texture that leaves no white marks, and lists 5% panthenol, madecassoside with copper, zinc and manganese, Tribioma and La Roche-Posay thermal spring water among its components [5].

Madecassoside is extracted from Centella asiatica, often shortened to 'cica' in skin care [5]. The brand takes its name from the spa town of La Roche-Posay in the Vienne department of western France [7]. The company is now part of L'Oréal's Dermatological Beauty division, which also includes CeraVe (bought by L'Oréal from Bausch Health in 2017) and Vichy [6].

sections.h: Ingredients and how the brand says it works
paras: Panthenol is a precursor of vitamin B5 that the brand describes as soothing and helping to repair skin barrier function [5]. Madecassoside is described as soothing and supporting epidermal renewal, and Tribioma as a complex of sugars, plant extracts and ferments meant to rebalance the microbiome of fragile skin, a claim the brand bases on in vitro testing [5]. These are manufacturer descriptions of the formula's intent, not findings from the independent studies below.
Users describe the practical effect as less tightness and flaking on irritated skin after it is applied.

Documented uses include superficial wounds, irritative dermatitis, soothing care after irritating treatments such as those for actinic keratosis, and care after dermatological procedures [1]. The NECOM oncodermatology group lists it among products in a supportive regimen for patients with cancer-treatment skin reactions alongside a gentle cleanser, moisturizer and sunscreen [4].

The brand states that it has been tested on 14 skin conditions, including post-procedure care, dryness, insect bites, discomfort related to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and irritation in babies' skin folds [5]. It recommends applying it generously to clean, dry skin twice a day, avoiding the eye contour, and says specific needs may call for more frequent use as directed by a dermatologist [5].

The appearance chain people describe is: a barrier-supporting balm calms irritated skin, visible redness and flaking fall, and the surface looks smoother and more even. Because retinoid users often experience dryness and flaking, and because peels, lasers and shaving leave skin temporarily sensitive, a balm of this kind is used to keep skin comfortable and presentable while it recovers.

On looksmax.org, La Roche-Posay products are common in basic routines. One routine posted there pairs a gentle cleanser, vitamin C and sunscreen in the morning with a tretinoin step and a Cicaplast lip balm at night, and a reply asks whether daily tretinoin leaves skin dry [3]. Other threads follow La Roche-Posay sunscreen releases, such as a UVA-focused reformulation, reflecting the brand's wider presence in community skincare [2].

A 2025 observational study in 2,337 patients with skin lesions requiring regenerative care found significant improvement in clinical and quality-of-life measures after use of Cicaplast Baume B5+; at least 64.9 percent of patients improved by at least one grade on each clinical symptom [1]. The study enrolled patients with superficial wounds, irritative dermatitis, skin needing soothing after treatments such as those for actinic keratosis, and skin after dermatological procedures [1].

A 2025 set of real-world cases from Nordic cutaneous oncodermatology experts reported that patients prescribed a regimen including Cicaplast Baume B5+ had less severe and less symptomatic skin reactions during cancer treatment [4]. The authors note that the regimen's products were tested for tolerance in patients undergoing cancer treatment [4].

The brand reports its own tests: an instrumental barrier-repair test in 26 subjects, a four-week study in 52 babies aged 4 to 34 months, and a seven-day study in 42 adults aged 18 to 68 after laser treatment, in which 60 percent said redness disappeared more quickly [5]. These are manufacturer-reported results.

The balm is designed for sensitive skin, and the 2025 study assessed tolerance alongside efficacy [1]. The brand advises avoiding the eye contour, not swallowing the product and keeping it away from babies and young children, and lists a 6-month shelf life after opening [5]. As with any cosmetic, individual reactions can occur, and some people find rich balm textures heavy on oily or acne-prone skin. Deep, infected or non-healing wounds are managed by clinicians rather than by cosmetic balms.

timeline.event: L'Oréal acquires CeraVe from Bausch Health, joining La Roche-Posay in its Dermatological Beauty division.[6]
European Journal of Dermatology publishes a 2,337-patient study of Cicaplast Baume B5+ in skin needing regenerative care.[1]
Journal of Drugs in Dermatology publishes NECOM real-world cases using a regimen that includes the balm for cancer-treatment skin reactions.[4]
